title: What is an LLM?

basics.say: LLM stands for Large Language Model. It's the engine inside chat assistants like ChatGPT, Claude or Copilot.
At its core, it plays one game: guess what comes next. 'The cat sat on the…' – what would you say?
It weighs every option. 'Mat' is very likely, 'sofa' less so, 'moon' almost never.
It picks one, adds it to the sentence and plays again – word after word – until a whole answer appears.
'Large' because it learned from a huge library of text. That's how guessing the next word turns into explaining, writing and translating.

deeper.say: Strictly speaking, it predicts tokens – small chunks of text – rather than whole words. That's our next topic.
What it learned is stored in billions of numbers called parameters, tuned during training so its guesses match real text.
After that first training, people teach it to follow instructions and be helpful. That's what turns a text predictor into an assistant.
On its own, it doesn't remember past chats or browse the web – apps add those as extra features. It works with what's in front of it.

takeaway: An LLM writes by predicting the next piece of text, again and again.
